entries.title: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS - 112)
entries.content: Under the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS), 112 is the single pan-India emergency number for citizens in distress. ERSS integrates police, fire, health/ambulance, and other emergency services into a unified platform. In immediate danger or life-threatening situations, individuals can dial 112 from any phone (even without balance or SIM in some networks) or trigger panic alerts via the 112 India mobile app. Emergency calls are routed to State Emergency Response Centres (ERC) which dispatch the nearest emergency response vehicle using Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) and GPS tracking. For urgent distress, calling 112 is the primary official mechanism in India.
entries.sourceName: Emergency Response Support System, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India

entries.title: Free Legal Aid for Women and Weaker Sections (NALSA)
entries.content: Under Section 12(c) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, every woman is entitled to free legal services regardless of her financial status or income. Free legal aid is provided through the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), State Legal Services Authorities (SLSA), District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA), and Taluk Legal Services Committees (TLSC). Entitlement includes provision of an advocate at state expense, drafting of legal pleadings, exemption from court fees, and assistance in civil, criminal, and matrimonial disputes. Eligible persons can contact the national legal aid toll-free helpline number 15100 or submit an application online or in person at the nearest DLSA or TLSC.

entries.title: Registration of First Information Report (FIR) under Section 173 of BNSS, 2023
entries.content: Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), every piece of information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing and read over to the informant. Information may also be given electronically (e-FIR), provided it is taken on record after being signed within three days by the person giving it. Under Section 173(1), an FIR can be registered irrespective of the territorial jurisdiction where the offence occurred (commonly termed Zero FIR), which is subsequently transferred to the police station having jurisdiction. A copy of the information recorded under Section 173 shall be given forthwith, free of cost, to the informant or the victim.
entries.sourceName: India Code, Ministry of Law and Justice

entries.title: Reliefs and Protection Orders under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entries.content: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (PWDVA), an aggrieved woman or a Protection Officer on her behalf may present an application to the Judicial Magistrate under Section 12 seeking one or more reliefs. Reliefs available under the Act include Protection Orders prohibiting acts of domestic violence or communication (Section 18), Residence Orders preventing eviction from the shared household (Section 19), Monetary Relief for medical expenses, loss of earnings, or maintenance (Section 20), Custody Orders for children (Section 21), and Compensation Orders for injuries and mental distress (Section 22). Aggrieved women may also seek assistance from designated Protection Officers, Service Providers, or approach the nearest DLSA for free legal assistance.
entries.sourceName: India Code, Ministry of Law and Justice

entries.title: Internal and Local Committee Redressal under POSH Act, 2013
entries.content: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act), any workplace employing 10 or more employees must constitute an Internal Committee (IC) under Section 4, headed by a Presiding Officer who is a senior woman employee. For workplaces with fewer than 10 employees or where the complaint is against the employer, complaints are handled by the Local Committee (LC) constituted by the District Officer under Section 6. An aggrieved woman may submit a written complaint within three months from the date of the incident (extendable by up to three months if justifiable circumstances prevented timely submission). Before initiating an inquiry under Section 11, the Committee may, at the request of the aggrieved woman, take steps to settle the matter through conciliation under Section 10, though no monetary settlement can form the basis of conciliation.
entries.sourceName: India Code, Ministry of Law and Justice

entries.title: Stalking and Outraging Modesty under Sections 78 and 79 of BNS, 2023
entries.content: Under Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman, or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email, or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking. Under Section 79 of the BNS, whoever intending to insult the modesty of any woman utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished. Victims may report these offences to the police via FIR under Section 173 of BNSS.
entries.sourceName: India Code, Ministry of Law and Justice

entries.title: Women Helpline (181 Scheme)
entries.content: The Women Helpline (WHL) universalized 24-hour toll-free telecom service accessible by dialing 181 is an initiative of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India. The helpline provides integrated support and assistance to women affected by violence, both in private and public spaces. It facilitates immediate crisis response by coordinating with emergency services like ERSS-112, Police, Hospitals, and Ambulance services, and provides referral linkages to One Stop Centres (OSCs), District Legal Services Authorities (DLSAs), and protection officers for medical, legal, and counseling aid.
entries.sourceName: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India

entries.title: Document Checklist for Approaching Legal Aid and Filing Complaints
entries.content: When approaching Legal Services Authorities (DLSA or TLSC) or filing a complaint before legal authorities, having pertinent documentation helps process the request efficiently. Helpful items include: (1) Identity and residence proof (such as Aadhaar card, Voter ID, or Ration card); (2) A clear written summary of events describing dates, times, locations, and involved parties; (3) Relevant supporting evidence (such as photographs, medical reports or injury certificates if physical harm occurred, electronic evidence including text messages, emails, or call logs); (4) Previous complaint copies, notices, or police acknowledgment slips if prior reports were submitted; and (5) Income certificate or affidavit of eligibility where applicable (note: women, children, and custody victims do not need income proof under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act).
